payload.text: The two versions of Form 4-H give different beneficial-ownership thresholds. The governing Arabic text (Appendix A, declaration First) says 10% or more of capital or voting rights. The English convenience translation (Appendix B) says 25% or more. ADD-03 8.2 says the Arabic text governs, so each member must list every natural person at 10% or more. A form completed on the English 25% threshold could be incomplete, and an incomplete Form 4-H makes the Proposal non-responsive (ADD-03 8.4). Complete Form 4-H on the 10% threshold. A clarification may be raised if the Bid manager wishes, but the governing text is clear.

entry.topic: permit/table interpretation (rolling averages in the 30-day reliability run)

sources.words: PCOD shall not be certified until the Facility has completed a continuous reliability run of thirty (30) days at not less than 90% of nominal capacity, during which every parameter in Table 2-4 has been met.
A failure of any Table 2-4 parameter during the reliability run shall restart the run in full.
compliance assessed as a 30-day rolling average unless stated
delay liquidated damages at the rate of one-twentieth of one per cent (0.05%) of the Estimated Project Cost for each day of delay

entry.gap: Most Table 2-4 parameters are assessed as 30-day rolling averages. VOL-II 7.2 and 7.3 do not say how such a parameter is 'met', or what counts as 'a failure', within a 30-day run. It could be an average over the run, a daily rolling value using pre-run data, or individual samples.
entry.practical_impact: A failure restarts the full 30 days. PCOD timing drives delay liquidated damages, now 0.05% of the Estimated Project Cost for each day of delay (VOL-V 18.1 as amended by ADD-03 4.1), which scales with the cost the Bidder states in Form 4-F. It also drives the 365-day termination right (VOL-V 18.3). The commissioning programme and float therefore depend on the answer.
entry.proposed_question: Volume II, Clauses 7.2 and 7.3, page 4: For Table 2-4 parameters whose basis of assessment is a 30-day rolling average, how is compliance determined during the 30-day reliability run (in particular, is the rolling average calculated over the run period only, or for each day of the run using data from before it began), and what constitutes 'a failure' of such a parameter for the purposes of Clause 7.3?
entry.interim_handling: Plan commissioning so that individual samples meet the rolling-average limits before the run starts. Hold programme float for at least one full restart, and price delay exposure at 0.05% of the Estimated Project Cost per day. Record both as programme assumptions.

evidence.words: delay liquidated damages at the rate of one-twentieth of one per cent (0.05%) of the Estimated Project Cost for each day of delay

The marks per criterion are settled: A 25, B 15, C 20, D 20, E 10, F 10, G 20.
entry.practical_impact: Determines how the technical narrative is weighted across criteria, including the new criterion G. It also sets the margin needed above the threshold of 70% of 120 marks (a Proposal below it does not proceed to commercial evaluation), and how price becomes the 30% commercial score.
entry.proposed_question: Addendum No. 3, Section 6, Note (3) to Table 1-1 (second revision), page 2: (a) What is the Authority's standard five-point scale, and how is a score on that scale converted into the marks shown in Table 1-1 (second revision), including for the threshold of seventy per cent (70%) of the total marks available in Volume I Clause 11.3 (page 5) as amended, given that the table shows marks rather than weights? (b) By what method is the commercial score calculated for the 30% commercial weighting in Volume I Clause 11.2 (page 5) as amended?
entry.interim_handling: Write to the marks per criterion (A 25, B 15, C 20, D 20, E 10, F 10, G 20; total 120) and aim for a clear margin above 84 marks. Treat the commercial formula as unknown and test price sensitivity without assuming one.
